Same-family test is same_family(a, b): name_key(a.head.name) == name_key(b.head.name) and a.head.birth_year == b.head.birth_year.", "file": "registry/dedup.py"}, {"id": "R2", "statement": "name_key(name: str) -> tuple[str, ...] is tuple(soundex(part) for part in name.split()); soundex(word) is American Soundex, first letter plus three digits (e.g. 'Robert' -> 'R163'), so 'Mohamed Ali' and 'Muhammad Ali' produce the same key.", "file": "registry/dedup.py"}, {"id": "R3", "statement": "find_duplicates only considers households with h.status == 'active' and sorts them by h.id; it groups by comparing each household to group[0].", "file": "registry/dedup.py"}, {"id": "R4", "statement": "is_valid_household_id(household_id: str) -> bool in core/ids.py validates IDs of the form HH-NNNNC via re.fullmatch(r\"HH-(\\d{4})(\\d)\") and household_check_digit(m.group(1)) == int(m.group(2)). Use this to pick the record with the valid ID.", "file": "core/ids.py"}, {"id": "R5", "statement": "household_check_digit(base: str) -> int | None computes a mod-11 check digit with CHECK_WEIGHTS = (5, 4, 3, 2) over the four base digits; returns None when the result would be 10 (such bases are never issued). Raises ValueError if base is not exactly 4 digits.", "file": "core/ids.py"}, {"id": "R6", "statement": "Household ID format is HH-NNNNC (four digits plus one check digit); make_household_id(number: int) -> str builds it and raises ValueError for bases with no valid check digit.", "file": "core/ids.py"}, {"id": "R7", "statement": "set_status(household_id: str, status: str, *, merged_into: str | None = None) -> Household in registry/register.py is the existing way to mark a record merged: it validates status in ('active', 'inactive', 'merged'), sets h.status and h.merged_into on the matching record, saves the whole list, and returns the Household. Raises KeyError if the ID is not found. This changes only the targeted record, satisfying 'no other record is changed'.", "file": "registry/register.py"}, {"id": "R8", "statement": "load_households(*, active_only: bool = False) -> list[Household] reads data/registry.json (key 'households') via store.read_json and returns Household objects; active_only filters to status == 'active'. save_households(households) writes the whole list back with store.write_json (atomic tmp-file + os.replace).", "file": "registry/register.py"}, {"id": "R9", "statement": "Household model fields: id, region, site, phone, members (members[0] is the head, with .head and .size properties), registered (ISO date), status ('active' | 'inactive' | 'merged', default 'active'), sms_ok, shelter_damaged, income_lost, disability, merged_into (str | None). Household.from_dict(d) / to_dict() convert to/from the JSON dicts.", "file": "core/models.py"}, {"id": "R10", "statement": "Double rations come from distribution: distribution/planner.py line 32 iterates load_households(active_only=True), so every active duplicate gets its own allocation. Marking duplicates as 'merged' (not deleting them) removes them from allocation while keeping the record.", "file": "distribution/planner.py"}, {"id": "R11", "statement": "Script conventions: ops scripts live in scripts/ and are run from the Lifeline root as `python scripts/<name>.py`; they must add the repo root to sys.path via sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent)) before importing project modules. Scripts that change data/registry.json or data/ledger.json must say so in their docstring.", "file": "scripts/stock_report.py"}, {"id": "R12", "statement": "store.py has no function to edit or delete records in append-only files, but registry.json is mutable: 'read, change, write back whole' via store.read_json / store.write_json. No record needs to be deleted for this ticket; set_status handles the merge marking.", "file": "core/store.py"}]}}
